    opponents = observation.get('opponents', [])
    # Territory Control
    territory = observation.get('territory', [])
    # Defensive checks
    if resource_positions:
        # Move towards the closest resource
        closest_res = min(resource_positions, key=lambda r: abs(r[0]-x)+abs(r[1]-y))
        dx = (closest_res[0] - x > 0) - (closest_res[0] - x < 0)
        dy = (closest_res[1] - y > 0) - (closest_res[1] - y < 0)
        return [dx, dy]
    elif opponents:
        # Pursuit / Evasion based on simple heuristic: evading if opponent is close
        for opp in opponents:
            ox, oy = opp.get('position', (x, y))
            dist = abs(ox - x) + abs(oy - y)

                # Evade: move away from opponent
                dx = (x - ox > 0) - (x - ox < 0)
                dy = (y - oy > 0) - (y - oy < 0)
                # Limit movement to -1,0,1
                dx = max(-1, min(1, dx))
                dy = max(-1, min(1, dy))
                return [dx, dy]
        # If opponents are far, approach the closest
        closest_opp = min(opponents, key=lambda o: abs(o.get('position', (x,y))[0] - x)+abs(o.get('position', (x,y))[1] - y))
        ox, oy = closest_opp.get('position', (x, y))
        dx = (ox - x > 0) - (ox - x < 0)
        dy = (oy - y > 0) - (oy - y < 0)
        return [dx, dy]
    elif territory:
        # Move towards own territory or expand
        # For simplicity, pick cell in territory that is closest
        # assuming agent is not on territory
        min_dist = float('inf')
        target = None
        for tx, ty in territory:
            dist = abs(tx - x) + abs(ty - y)

                target = (tx, ty)

            dy = (target[1] - y > 0) - (target[1] - y < 0)
            return [dx, dy]

    # Default: stay still
    return [0, 0]
